title: Finally mastery: The SECRET to landing the TBM 930 perfectly
description:
The TBM 930 short‑field landing, Beta range technique, and PT6 shutdown are the focus of this final MSFS 2024 tutorial.  
This TBM 930 descent and energy‑management guide brings everything together as we wrap up the series.

Welcome to the finale of our six‑week TBM 930 journey. Today we tackle the “slippery” descent, the Beta range secret for short runways, and the correct PT6 cool‑down procedure every turbine pilot must know. If you’ve followed the series, this episode completes your full TBM workflow from startup to shutdown.

📖 Chapters
In this video, we cover:

0:00 - Intro: bringing it home 
1:23 - Energy management: The "slippery" descent
7:40 - Vertical navigation: the 'VNAV' handover
7:43 - The Descent: VNAV & Top of Descent (TOD) 
13:24 - Final configuration: the 'Approaching' capture
18:46 - The flare & the 'beta' stop
23:02 - Final taxi: the 'chock and chain' arrival
25:43 - Shutdown: cooling the core
30:54 - "Nice to know": The TBM's secret door
31:57 - Series wrap-up:you are a TBM pilot

📷 Quick camera views
- shift 1: primary flight display (PFD)
- shift 2: multi function display (MFD)
- shift 3: autopilot controls
- shift 4: overview of PFD, MFD, autopilot controls, A/C, de ice system, landing gear,  pressurization and hot air flow
- shift 5: throttle, trim, flap controls and fuel selector
- shift 6: external/internal lights, electric power, engine start, fuel, ap/trims, ELT and oxygen controls
- shift 7: similar like the previous option but including the panel emer
- shift 8: power plugs
- shift 9: left door
- shift 0: passenger door
